dataset.description: Experimental data coming from physico-chemical analysis of milk and cheese samples from commercial farms. Compositional analyses include gross composition, mineral elements, fatty acids, tocols, terpenoids, biogenic amines and antibiotic residues.
keyword: Physico-chemical composition of milk and cheese
dataset.title: Data on physico-chemical analysis of milk and cheese samples

dataset.description: Experimental data coming from genomic  and  metagenomic analysis of milk and cheese samples from commercial farms. Analyses include microbial populations and antibiotic resistance genes.
keyword: Genomic and metagenomic analysis of milk and cheese
Genomic analysis of milk and cheese
dataset.title: Data on genomic and metagenomic analysis of milk and cheese samples

dataset.description:
Socio-economic and technical-productive data are recorded by the farmers using digital questionaires.Two digital questionaries are used: (1) livestock activity records, and (2) incomes and expenses records. Livestock activity records are professional activity, work seasons, farm size and facilities, and family help and workers hiring. Income records are animal and food production, sales, subsidies and other incomes. Expenses records are animal feed, veterinary and other supplies, energy and water consumption, facilities and machinery maintenance, rental and other expenses.

Likewise, data contain personal information of commercial farmers participating in the proyect (name and family name, telephone, email, farm address).
keyword: Socio-economic and technical-productive records of farms
dataset.title: Data on socio-economic and technical-productive records of commercial farms

dataset.description: Experimental data coming from sensory assays with consumers related to acceptability of cheese samples . Sensory data are flavour, odour and texture attributes of cheese samples. Consumer informations (demographic, social, cultural, consumption practices and sustainable assessment on  food production systems) are also recorded using questionaries. Likewise, data contain personal information of consumers participating in the acceptabiliy study (name, telephone, email, town or city of residence, age, sex and others).
dataset.title: Data on sensory acceptability assays with consumers

dataset.description: Data coming from the description of grassland plots on commercial farms, and from the analysis of vegetation and soil samples collected in these plots. Plot description is based on the number, size, type, location and farmer management (grazing, mowing, mixed). Vegetation analyses include floristic composition based on the relative abundances of plant species and diversity of sampled plots, along with assessments of nutritional quality (carbon, nitrogen, phosphorous, potassium, calcium, magnesium, neutral detergent fiber and digestibility) of grassland samples. Soil analysis include microbiota composition and diversity (bacteria and fungi), as well as physico-chemical properties (pH, texture, nutrients, soil organic carbon).
keyword: Grassland plots and vegetation and soil analysis
Plot records and vegetation and soil analysis
dataset.title: Data on grassland plots and analysis of vegetation and soil samples

dmp.description:
ExtenSheep project is part of LiveSheep coordinated project and both share the hypothesis that the optimal degree of extensification of dairy sheep systems depends on their adaptation to the environmental and socioeconomic demands. This hypothesis implies that a multidisciplinary perspective is necessary to assess the sustainability of dairy sheep systems. This multidisciplinary perspective allows the shape of new socioeconomic and biophysical indicators to identify critical trade-offs decisive for farm sustainability. The assessment of farm resilience and sustainability will address at multiple scales the associated trade-offs between socioeconomic, environmental, technical-productive, animal welfare, and food quality and safety dimensions.

The purpose of the DMP for this project is to manage different types of data depending on their nature and origin.These data come from the following different methodological approachs: (1) experimental data coming from physico-chemical analysis of milk and cheese samples from commercial farms; (2) experimental data coming from genomic and metagenomic analysis of milk and cheese samples from commercial farms; (3) experimental data coming from vegetation surveys, physico-chemical and metagenomic analysis of soil samples from grassland plots belonged to commercial farms;  (4) experimental data coming from sensory aceptability assays with consumers; and (5) socio-economic and technical-productive data coming from survey in commercial farms.
